findings.comment: Overhead electric lines exist on the property (shown on Sheet 4 existing survey), and buildings are proposed (Sheets 9, 21). However, no surveyed conductor elevations or horizontal clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to any building faces are provided. Measurement from conductor location (not pole centerline) required to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance cannot be determined without surveyor data showing conductor position relative to building setbacks.

Distribution overhead conductors shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4); buildings and facilities proposed throughout site (Sheets 9, 21). Without surveyed conductor locations and radial clearance dimensions, the 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor in all directions cannot be verified. No profile drawings show radial clearance envelopes.

applicableAreas: Building projections where overhead facilities present
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet plan set, preventing verification of overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, or patios relative to overhead conductors. Both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances for building projections cannot be assessed.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1 and 2 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way
findings.comment: Overhead utility lines exist in the right-of-way along Valley View Road (western boundary per Sheet 4), and buildings are proposed within potential clearance distance (Sheet 9). No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions from outside conductor to buildings are provided, preventing verification of required 7.5-foot and 15-foot clearances.

Building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not included in the submitted site plan. The 39-sheet plan set contains no building elevation drawings. Per UCM § 1.10.3, engineered, sealed elevation drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and buildings, including all projections, with dimensioned clearances are required.

Site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical design plan (Sheet 21) show building locations and site features, but contain no dimension lines or annotations showing distances from outer electric conductors to building edges, projections, or other site features. Required section views and enlarged plan details with dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location are not provided.

applicableAreas: Proposed fence post locations throughout property perimeter
findings.comment: Fences are proposed (noted on landscape plan Sheet 31 and landscape calculations Sheet 35), including wooden privacy fences. Existing utility poles are shown on the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) at multiple property boundaries. Without exact measured distances between proposed fence post locations and existing pole locations, the 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls throughout site perimeter and around detention pond
findings.comment: Retaining walls are detailed on Sheets 38-39, and overhead electric facilities exist on property boundaries (Sheet 4). However, no dimension lines or clearance annotations show distances from the outside conductor to the outermost edge of any retaining wall. Horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to wall faces cannot be verified without surveyor data and section exhibits.

applicableAreas: Internal driveways, parking areas with overhead electric line proximity
findings.comment: Internal driveways and parking areas are proposed (Sheets 9, 11). Overhead utility lines exist on property boundaries (Sheet 4). No vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attachments) to finished driveway/parking grades are provided. Verification of 16-foot minimum (parking without trucks) or 18-foot (areas with truck traffic) clearance requires surveyed conductor elevation data and grading section exhibits not provided.

Dimension lines and clearance annotations on submitted plans show distances from property lines, easement boundaries, and pole locations, but do not originate from the outside conductor location. Per UCM § 1.10.3 and the measurement methodology in the regulatory overview, all clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline or easement boundaries. On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension lines must explicitly show origin at conductor position.

applicableAreas: Public sidewalk along Valley View Road right-of-way, property end locations
findings.comment: Existing utility poles are shown on Sheet 4 along the western property line within right-of-way. A public sidewalk is proposed along Valley View Road frontage (Sheet 9). Without dimensioned drawings showing exact clearance distances from sidewalk location to pole positions at each property end along right-of-way, the requirement cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, all site features, electric easement areas
findings.comment: Overhead distribution lines and electric easements (5-foot easements) are shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4). Buildings are positioned within electric easement areas on the site plan (Sheet 9). Without surveyed conductor routing and exact clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to all buildings and site features within the easement, it cannot be definitively verified that customer facilities are not installed beneath or over distribution conductors (absolute prohibition per UCM § 1.10.3) or that 7.5-foot clearance is maintained for items within easements.

applicableAreas: All structures with potential overhead conductor clearance concerns
findings.comment: No registered surveyor data showing pole locations and mid-span conductor clearances is provided on any submitted sheet. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows surveyed pole locations, but no conductor elevation data. When overhead facilities cross proposed site features (buildings, driveways, parking), surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are required to verify vertical clearances meet minimum requirements. These measurements are absent from the plan set.

applicableAreas: Landscape areas near overhead electric line on southern property boundary
findings.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees (marked M for Mitigation and PL for Parking Lot types) positioned within approximately 10-15 feet of the overhead electric line on the southern property boundary. The landscape calculations (Sheet 35) provide a plant list (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but the specific tree species cannot be cross-referenced to the landscape plan location symbols. Without confirmed species identification for the trees near the overhead line, utility-compatible status cannot be verified against ECM Appendix F. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors must be utility-compatible species (generally mature height ≤20 feet marked UC).
